newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz open to talks with French Jews on boycott.
newsitem.headline: Allianz open to talks with French Jews on boycott.

text.p: Allianz AG Holding said on Monday it was ready to talk with France's Jewish community after a U.S. lawsuit alleged that the German insurer had benefited from Nazi persecution of Jews.
A French Jewish group had earlier called for a boycott of Allianz.
"We have always said that we are open for discussion and that goes as well for the Jewish community in France," a spokesman said.
The FFDJF association of descendants of French Jews deported to death camps called on the public not to take out an insurance policy with Allianz until the group took steps to compensate victims.

Allianz has launched a campaign to help relatives of Holocaust victims track down missing assets after it was named with six other insurers in a class-action lawsuit launched earlier this year in the United States.
The suit alleges that insurers concealed or converted the cash value and proceeds of insurance policies sold before 1946 to mainly Jewish victims of Nazi persecution.
The allegations are similar to those made against some Swiss banks alleged to have profited from the Hitler regime.
"It is certainly not good news. It came as a bit of a surprise especially as they picked the one company that has tried to confront this issue," the spokesman said.
Allianz said it had not been informed officially of the boycott call and was not aware of any protest actions being taken at its French outlets.

"We don't know what the effects will be," the spokesman said, adding that Allianz had annual premium income of around 2.9 billion marks ($1.7 billion) from its French business after currency translation.
The Allianz group has total premium income of 74.6 billion marks. ($ = 1.713 German Marks)
